Package io.mavlink4j.session

Interface PeerDirectory

public interface PeerDirectory
Who is out there — read-only protocol facts, updated by MavlinkSession as frames arrive. Deliberately carries no ownership or access logic: which sysid a host's device owns is host policy, not a protocol fact, and belongs to the calling application. This interface only ever answers "what has been observed," never "who is allowed to use it."

    • concurrentAddresses

      Set<LinkPeer> concurrentAddresses(PeerId id, Duration window)
      The source addresses id is concurrently transmitting from: on any one link, the addresses each heard within the last window, provided there are two or more of them (otherwise nothing is reported for that link). That is the signature of two vehicles sharing one sysid; peer(io.mavlink4j.PeerId) keeps only the newest address, so this is the one place the other is still visible.

      Counted per link on purpose: one vehicle heard on two links (a UDP carrier and a serial radio, a failover pair) has one address per link and is not a conflict. And window is a concurrency window, not a silence window: a vehicle that reboots and comes back from a new source port stops being heard at the old one, so the two never overlap for long. Empty when no link has two such addresses.
